title: Active learning improved whole-cell antibiotic screening and validation
summary: A closed-loop active-learning campaign for Borrelia burgdorferi whole-cell screening increased the experimental hit rate five-fold, from 0.2% in investigator-selected plates to 1.0% in the AL-guided campaign. The same study separately reports prospective in-silico selection of diverse compounds across bacterial species, with 11.0% experimental validation of predicted hits and 53-fold enrichment over investigator-directed screening; those validated compounds showed the intended narrow-spectrum B. burgdorferi activity. These are assay and screening results, not clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: Active learning using a directed message-passing neural network and evidential Dirichlet head
organization: Harvard Medical School; Tufts University; Tufts Lyme Disease Initiative; Texas A&M University; Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; Tufts University School of Medicine; Stuart B. Levy Center for Integrated Management of Antimicrobial Resistance; Tufts University School of Engineering; Mass General Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv indexed text, PubMed metadata/abstract and PMC indexed full-text excerpt; direct bioRxiv and PMC page loads were blocked.

evidence.tested: In a closed-loop Borrelia burgdorferi campaign, active-learning-guided selection produced a 1.0% experimental screening hit rate versus 0.2% in investigator-selected plates. A separate prospective in-silico selection across bacterial species achieved 11.0% experimental validation of predicted hits (53-fold enrichment over investigator-directed screening); the paper reports intended narrow-spectrum activity for B. burgdorferi.
evidence.unknown: Preprint evidence is not independent replication or clinical testing. The cross-species hit-validation experiment is distinct from the closed-loop Borrelia hit-rate comparison. Direct full page retrieval was blocked; checked material was the primary indexed preprint and archived primary article text.
evidence.ai_role: A directed message-passing neural network with an evidential Dirichlet head supported active-learning compound selection for whole-cell inhibition testing; selected compounds were then experimentally screened.
